propositions: A failed or timed-out tickets-branch fetch causes rebar init to silently create an empty divergent orphan store instead of failing closed.
Branch-existence checks rely only on local refs and remote-tracking refs, so an unreachable remote is indistinguishable from a genuine first init.
A shared tri-state remote-branch probe using git ls-remote --exit-code must distinguish advertised, reachable-absent, and unreachable states across all four consumers.
When the remote advertises the branch but fetch fails, init must return nonzero without creating an orphan branch.
When the remote is unreachable or times out, init fails closed with a distinct diagnostic unless an explicit --force-new-store override is supplied.
The tri-state probe result is cached under a short TTL keyed by repo, remote, and branch so one CLI invocation performs at most one probe.
